review_notes: Reviewed all 75 lines of the target and the imported spectral-path definitions, as well as the mathlib projection-to-interval source for the proposed replacement lemma. The monotonicity proof contains a direct recreation of an available, named lemma; I found no other proof simplification clearly better for readability.

findings.excerpt:
have hc : (Set.projIcc 0 1 zero_le_one s : ℝ) ≤ (Set.projIcc 0 1 zero_le_one t : ℝ) :=
    max_le_max le_rfl (min_le_min le_rfl hst)
findings.problem: This manually proves monotonicity of `Set.projIcc` by unfolding its max/min construction. Mathlib provides a named monotonicity lemma for the projection, so the intermediate calculation can be removed while keeping the reason the projected endpoints are ordered explicit.
findings.proposed_change: Replace the `have hc` block with `have hc : (Set.projIcc 0 1 zero_le_one s : ℝ) ≤ (Set.projIcc 0 1 zero_le_one t : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast Set.monotone_projIcc zero_le_one hst`. The following integral comparison can remain unchanged.
findings.benefit: The proof uses the library theorem matching the mathematical step—projection preserves order—instead of exposing its implementation as nested `max` and `min`. This is shorter without obscuring the argument.

evidence.excerpt:
theorem monotone_projIcc : Monotone (projIcc a b h) := fun _ _ hxy =>
  max_le_max le_rfl <| min_le_min le_rfl hxy
